newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco says excavations show sedentary life in Sahara.
newsitem.headline: Morocco says excavations show sedentary life in Sahara.

text.p: Archaeologists have unearthed remains of walls and fortresses in the Western Sahara, substantiating evidence of a thriving sedentary civilisation there, the Moroccan official news agency MAP said on Wednesday.

The excavations showed that several fortresses had dotted the Atlantic coast in the region giving ancient inhabitants control of coastal waters as well as inland plains in the now mostly barren desert areas, said MAP.

"The (archaeologic) research in Naaila (near the main city of Laayoune), which started just two weeks ago...has already resulted in finding the remains of ancient cemeteries and springs and other vestiges which has an historical importance," MAP added.
Morocco and the Polisario Front fought a 16-year desert war in the Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony, before they agreed on a ceasefire in 1991, as part of a U.N.-sponsored peace plan.
The future status of the territory, mostly controlled by Morocco, still has to be decided.
